new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not contrastive; by Laycock's transcription default it falls on the first syllable of the word whose vowel is not schwa (word-initial unless the first syllable has [ə], in which case the next full-vowel syllable). No Yis form in his list departs from this default.
new_statements.exceptions: Syllables containing schwa [ə] are skipped: stress falls on the first non-schwa syllable (e.g. təfau, kəmiene, nəfkayə would be stressed on the second syllable). Words whose stress is elsewhere would have been marked; none of the Yis forms is marked.
new_statements.domain_note: Survey-wide transcription convention for the isolated wordlist forms of all ~60 Lumi-Subdistrict languages, not a Yis-specific analysis; based on a short list elicited from one informant (Tepeiwa of Parisko) at Lumi in July 1967. Word-level, citation forms. Stress is explicitly called non-phonemic; under the convention an unmarked word is stressed on its first syllable whose vowel is not schwa, and the 45 re-keyed Yis forms on TransNewGuinea.org carry no stress mark.
new_statements.identity_note: Laycock's 'Yis' (1968 no. 7; 1973 entry 18; villages Kalingum, Kwatum, Timeni, Kernam, Parisko) = Glottolog yiss1240 / ISO yis exactly (Glottolog's language code mapping for ref 138610 gives 'Yis [yis]'). The stress statement, however, is survey-wide over all Lumi-Subdistrict languages, not a Yis-specific analysis; the informant was Tepeiwa of Parisko (S.W. Wapei CD), so if dialect matters the data are from the Parisko variety.
